narrative: The agent answered no thread inline; it posted batched disposition comments and worked findings from CoPirate and a private /code-review pane together. Seven findings were caused by incomplete or sloppy fixes to earlier threads: a containment claim fixed in bundle.go but not sbom.go, a gate fix covering one of three artifacts and one of three substitutions, a FORKS.md phrase skipped while its CHANGELOG twin was fixed, a wrong cross-reference written by a fix, and FORKS.md shipped without a gate proof. Many more were caused by off-thread fixes, mainly bfdb426's new ReplacedByVersion kind, which arrived without test entries, wording review, or a sweep of titles and legends. Every round also carried findings not caused by thread fixes, so no round was purely avoidable. Only F2 was declined, with a defensible carrying-cost argument.
guidance_observations: Fixes repeatedly corrected one instance of a phrase or claim while a twin elsewhere survived (bundle vs SBOM, CHANGELOG vs FORKS.md); grepping for the corrected phrase after each fix would have cut at least three findings.
The agent's disposition comment for round 2 declared 'This is the last round', and three more rounds followed, each finding real defects, so declaring convergence early was not borne out.

Adding a sum-type variant (ReplacedByVersion) mid-review spawned five follow-up findings (F11, F13, F14, F20, F26); a new variant should land with every consumer's test table and user-facing wording updated in the same commit.
F5 sat unfixed through two review rounds before 6d30e19, so the batched-disposition process let some threads slip until a later full-scope pass.
